trial_title: CRANIO-CAUDAL AND LATERAL APPROACH FOR RECURRENT LARYNGEAL NERVE
brief_summary: The recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) dissection should be performed cranio-caudally in TOETVA approach.The aim of this study was to compare the cranio-caudal and lateral approach for RLN dissection in regard with the rates of LOS during conventional thyroidectomy using continuous intraoperative nerve monitoring (CIONM).

eligibility_table.justification: The patient has metastatic papillary thyroid cancer, but the specific criterion of multinodular goitre is not clearly addressed in the profile.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a multinodular goitre confirmed by imaging studies?

eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a diagnosis of thyroid papillary cancer, which meets this inclusion criterion.
The patient has metastatic disease and prior treatments, indicating they do not have a solitary thyroid nodule.
The patient has a history of neck mass resection, which qualifies as previous thyroid surgery.
The profile does not provide information on the presence of a substernal goiter.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a substernal goiter as confirmed by imaging studies?

eligibility_table.justification: There is no information regarding preoperative vocal cord paralysis (VCP) in the patient's history.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a preoperative diagnosis of vocal cord paralysis (VCP) confirmed by laryngoscopy?

eligibility_table.criterion: evidence of lateral lymph node metastasis
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has evidence of metastatic disease to lymph nodes, which indicates lateral lymph node metastasis.

eligibility_table.criterion: intentional transection of the RLN due to tumor invasion
eligibility_table.justification: The profile does not specify whether there was intentional transection of the recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN).
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is there evidence of tumor invasion into the recurrent laryngeal nerve as determined by imaging studies or intraoperative findings?

eligibility_table.clinical_question: Was the intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) equipment fully functional and successfully utilized during the assessment of the recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) in this patient?
